presentation.label: FILTER BANK
presentation.summary: Ladder, SEM, isolator and vowel filters.
presentation.overview: Four filter voices in one FX1 slot. Move between a ladder filter, a SEM-style state-variable filter, an isolator and a vowel filter, with envelope and LFO modulation.
highlights: Ladder, SEM, isolator and vowel modes
usage: Choose SPECTRUM in FX1. MODE selects ladder, SEM, isolator or vowel filtering.
In SEM mode, SHPE moves between low-pass, band-pass and high-pass. FREQ controls cutoff; RES controls resonance.
Use ENV for envelope response and LDP / LSP for LFO modulation. Start with low resonance, then raise it while monitoring the output.

controls.name: FREQ
controls.doc: the cutoff, 60 Hz..15 kHz exponential; in VOWL the vowel A-E-I-O-U; ENV and LFO move it

controls.name: RES
controls.doc: the flavour: resonance in SEM/LADR, sharpness in VOWL, the dielectric colour in ISO

controls.name: ENV
controls.doc: the envelope follower onto the cutoff, drawn -64..+63; 0 = none

controls.name: LDP
controls.doc: LFO depth onto the cutoff, 0 = none (a negative depth would only flip the phase)

controls.name: LSP
controls.doc: LFO speed ~0.08..9 Hz, and the envelope release (0 slow .. 127 fast)

controls.name: WDTH
controls.doc: stereo width of the output, drawn -64..+63: 0 untouched, -64 mono, +63 double sides

controls.name: MODE
controls.doc: LADR the Moog (first); SEM the SVF (SHPE: LP -> BP -> HP); ISO (Capacitor2); VOWL

controls.name: SHPE
controls.doc: SEM only: 0 lowpass, 64 bandpass, 127 highpass, crossfaded; --- in the other modes

presentation.label: STEREO MOTION
presentation.summary: Chorus, dimension, flanger, phaser and comb.
presentation.overview: A collection of chorus, dimension, flanger, comb and phaser voices. Shape movement with rate and depth, then dial in feedback, tone and stereo width.
usage: Choose MODULATION in FX1, then select JUNO, DIM, FLNG, COMB or PHSR on the setup page.
RATE and DPTH control movement in the modulation modes. COMB uses DLY for pitch; RATE has no LFO role there.
FDBK is bipolar. MIX blends the effect, while TONE and WDTH shape brightness and stereo spread.

controls.name: RATE
controls.doc: LFO speed, 0.08 .. 10 Hz on a squared taper (26 = the Juno's 0.5 Hz)

controls.name: DPTH
controls.doc: the sweep, 0 .. 480 samples either side of DLY; in PHSR the LFO's reach

controls.name: DLY
controls.doc: the sweep's centre, 0.2 .. 23 ms; COMB's pitch; PHSR's stage count (2/4/6/8 by quarters)

controls.name: FDBK
controls.doc: bipolar, 64 = none: feedback from the swept tap; PHSR regen; COMB decay time and polarity

controls.name: LOFI
controls.doc: the line clocked coarse and quantised: hold 1 + 64 (k/128)^2 samples, 24 bits then 16..5

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: dry/wet; 0 = exact passthrough, 127 = the wet alone

controls.name: MODE
controls.doc: which pedal

controls.name: TONE
controls.doc: the BBD filters in and out of the line: 0 dark (2 kHz), 127 open; COMB brightness; no PHSR

controls.name: WDTH
controls.doc: the right channel LFO lag: 0 mono, 64 quadrature, 127 antiphase (Juno, DIM); not COMB

presentation.label: WAVE SHAPING
presentation.summary: Fold, saturation, tone, compression and width.
presentation.overview: A chain for adding weight, grit and control: wavefolding, saturation, tone, compression and stereo width. Tape, tube and inflator saturation give the drive stage three different characters.
usage: Choose CHARACTER in FX1. Its fixed chain is fold → saturate → tone → compress → width → mix.
SAT selects tape, tube or inflator character; DRV sets the drive amount. FOLD adds wavefolding before saturation.
KEY selects the compressor source. WDTH at 64 keeps the original width, 0 is mono. Start with MIX low when exploring stronger drive or fold.

controls.name: DRV
controls.doc: drive into the curve, +12 dB at 127 (TUBE/INFL output-compensated); 0 skips

controls.name: FOLD
controls.doc: wavefolder drive, 1x..48x into the fold at a held level; 0 = no folding

controls.name: WDTH
controls.doc: mid/side width, drawn -64..+63: 0 = untouched, -64 = mono, +63 = double the sides

controls.name: COMP
controls.doc: compression amount; 0 = no gain reduction at any level

controls.name: TONE
controls.doc: a tilt after the saturator in every mode: 64 flat, 127 bright, 0 dark

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: dry/wet across the whole chain; 0 = exact passthrough

controls.name: SAT
controls.doc: character: TAPE (TapeHead), TUBE (DaTube, asymmetric), INFL (OInflator). JClones, MIT

controls.name: KEY
controls.doc: the compressor's key: SELF = this track's input, T1 = T1's level (ignored on the master)

controls.name: KLVL
controls.doc: how hard T1 drives the compressor with KEY = T1: 64 = unity, 127 = x2

presentation.label: DIFFUSED SPACE
presentation.summary: A diffused reverb with a modulated tail.
presentation.overview: A compact diffused reverb with a modulated tail. Control its length and darkness, then use modulation depth and rate to add movement to the space.
usage: Choose MINI VERB in FX2. DECAY controls the tail; higher DAMP makes the sound darker.
MOD sets modulation depth and RATE selects one of eight modulation speeds. Use MIX to place the reverb behind the dry signal.
The delay ring clears progressively on initialization. Audio stays dry until the ring is ready.

presentation.label: SINGLE-HEAD ECHO
presentation.summary: A single-head echo with wow, flutter and tape age.
presentation.overview: A single-head tape echo with wow, randomized flutter and tape age. Explore drifting repeats, worn tape texture and feedback, with free or beat-synced timing.
usage: Choose TAPE ECHO in FX2. SYNC selects FREE timing or BEAT divisions; TIME adjusts the delay.
FDBK controls repeats, WOW adds pitch movement and flutter, and AGE changes bandwidth and tape noise. MIX controls dry/wet balance.
When migrating older projects, former HEADS locks now address AGE. Back up projects and review old effect defaults and parameter locks.

controls.name: TIME
controls.doc: FREE: 46..231 ms; BEAT: twelve note divisions from 1/64 to dotted 1/4

controls.name: FDBK
controls.doc: repeat intensity; the upper range safely self-oscillates from tape noise

controls.name: WOW
controls.doc: 0.8 Hz wow plus irregular flutter; about 8 cents at 44, 22 cents at 127

controls.name: AGE
controls.doc: repeat bandwidth, flutter and noise; fresh at 0, worn at 127

controls.name: SYNC
controls.doc: FREE uses milliseconds; BEAT quantises TIME from stock tempo

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: dry/wet crossfade; 0 is exact passthrough

presentation.label: RHYTHMIC FILTER
presentation.summary: Euclidean rhythms for filters and amplitude.
presentation.overview: Euclidean rhythms drive filter cutoff or amplitude. Set the number of steps and pulses, rotate the pattern, and shape each movement with the envelope controls.
highlights: LP, BP, HP, notch and amplitude modes
usage: Set STEPS for the pattern length and PULSE for the number of evenly distributed events.
ROT rotates the rhythm and RATE sets its time grid. TYPE selects low-pass, band-pass, high-pass, notch or amplitude modulation.
FREQ sets the base cutoff, DEPTH controls movement and DEC / LEN shapes each event. AMP mode relabels these controls for level and amount.

controls.name: FREQ
controls.doc: Base filter cutoff or AMP level; cutoff is 30 Hz..15 kHz logarithmic

controls.name: RES
controls.doc: Filter resonance; inert for AMP

controls.name: DEPTH
controls.doc: Cutoff or gain modulation: negative/down, zero/static, positive/up

controls.name: DECAY
controls.doc: Envelope decay up to eight steps / gate length; inert for random

controls.name: STEPS
controls.doc: Euclidean cycle length 1..64 (stored as length minus one)

controls.name: PULSE
controls.doc: Pulse count; values above STEPS are clamped to STEPS

controls.name: ROT
controls.doc: Shift rhythm and captured values right, modulo STEPS

controls.name: RATE
controls.doc: Division relative to the track speed; 1/16 = one track step

controls.name: TYPE
controls.doc: Two-pole low/high/band/notch filter response, or amplitude modulation

controls.name: ATK
controls.doc: Attack / gate edge / random slew, 0..one step

controls.name: OUT
controls.doc: Pulse envelope, timed gate, random sample-and-hold, captured random

controls.name: MIX
controls.doc: Dry/wet; zero is exact passthrough

presentation.label: TEMPO FOLLOW
presentation.summary: Follow project tempo by changing playback speed.
presentation.overview: Repitch adds a timestretch option for Flex and Static machines. The sample follows project tempo by changing playback speed, so pitch moves with the tempo.
highlights: Available for Flex and Static machines
usage: For a Flex or Static track, open SRC SETUP and choose RPCH in TSTR. Alternatively set the sample attribute to REPITCH and use AUTO on the track.
Playback speed follows project BPM divided by sample BPM. A 120 BPM loop at 90 BPM plays lower and lasts longer.
PTCH is disabled for Repitch, but RATE still applies. Pickup machines are not supported; sample tempo must be 30–300 BPM and playback speed is capped at 2×.
